top_3_developments.headline: Government watchdog and Congress investigated allegations of DOGE staffer misusing Social Security data
top_3_developments.summary: The Social Security Administration's inspector general notified congressional leaders on March 6, 2026, of an anonymous complaint regarding potential misuse of SSA data by a former DOGE employee, including retention of NUMIDENT and Death Master File databases. House Oversight Democrats demanded answers and investigations into DOGE's data access practices. This follows prior disclosures of DOGE's improper data sharing in 2025 and ongoing court fights over data abuse.

top_3_developments.headline: Schedule Policy Career reclassified ~50,000 federal positions to at-will amid hiring freeze thaw
top_3_developments.summary: As the federal hiring freeze ended in March 2026, OPM implemented Schedule Policy (SP) for policy-influencing GS-13+ roles, making them at-will with reduced protections, evolving from Schedule F. Schedule Career (SC) protects operational roles, with agencies prioritizing SC for stability while using SP for flexibility. OPM estimates 50,000 positions affected, focusing on grant-makers and policy staff; existing employees have reclassification options.

top_3_developments.headline: OPM proposed performance ratings over seniority for RIF retention in federal layoffs
top_3_developments.summary: On March 5, 2026, OPM proposed rules shifting RIF retention priority to three-year performance ratings after tenure group, demoting seniority to tiebreaker. Earlier February 24 proposal allows forced distribution in performance ratings. Changes support 'lean government' post-DOGE attrition.
